newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Oct 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move that is a first for Australian banks, Westpac Banking Corp yesterday embraced securitisation by matching the funding tactics of the mortgage managers, the banks' newest and most important lending competitors. The move by Westpac intensifies competition in Australia's A$50 billion home loan market. Page 1.

A dispute between Tabcorp Holdings and Sky Channel, owned by Kerry Packer and Rupert Murdoch, over the cost of race meetings will potentially flare into a block-out of the coverage of races in all Victorian TAB outlets today. The dispute has stemmed from Sky's 264 percent broadcasting fee increase and the racing industry's intention of establishing its own pay-TV channel. Page 1.

Telecommunications giant Telstra has announced plans to sell its chain of retail outlets as part of a massive cost-cutting exercise. The move will see the group shed up to 850 staff from the Telstra payroll. The withdrawal from retail operations reinforce Telstra's agenda to exit non-core business functions. Page 2.

In what could be classed as a benchmark deal, a standard 50-hour working week has been established for workers at Ravensworth Beef Pty Ltd in western New South Wales under a non-union workplace deal. The federal enterprise flexibility agreement involved private consultants who remain one of the architects of the government's Workplace Relations Bill. Page 2.

Figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics revealed a low current account deficit in August - boosting speculation that short-term interest rates could soon fall. The current account deficit for the month was A$1.33 billion - about a third lower than the average recorded during the previous three months. Page 5.

Automotive components group Pacific BBA Ltd will build its first factory in the U.S. following the announcement of a A$200 million contract to manufacture brake parts from the year 2001. Despite the project cost of A$100 million over the next few years, Pacific BBA is confident of handling the cost without needing to raise new capital. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

One of Australia's leading miners, WMC Ltd, yesterday issued its 1996 annual report, which warns the federal government that the company's already sharply curtailed spending on Australian greenfields mineral exploration will continue to decrease due to land access problems related to native title issues. Page 19.

Wang Yung-ching, one of the most powerful businessmen in Asia, sitting at the head of the Formosa Plastics Group - a conglomerate with annual revenues of more than A$13 billion - arrived in Australia yesterday in a visit which could lead to a big increase in Australian steaming coal and liquefied natural gas sales to Taiwan. Page 19.

While unanimous in the view that decelerating inflation, a soft labour market and slowing demand growth are enough to convince the Reserve Bank board, which meets today, to ease credit, most analysts believe the central bank board will decide not to drop official interest rates until later this month or early in November. Page 19.

Despite the International Monetary Fund's chief economic policy arm, the Interim Committee, delaying talks over any immediate action to alleviate the debt burden in many Third World nations, the IMF has urged nations to pursue both fiscal discipline and structural reform of their new economies as part of a new strategy to sustain low inflationary growth. Page 19.

Westpac Banking Corp has signed a A$340 million securitisation deal with French Bank Societe Generale, paving the way for Australian-based home loans being sold on international markets. Societe Generale has purchased a portfolio of Westpac's basic option home loans which will underpin new mortgage-backed securities. Page 20.

Freight group TNT Ltd will remove the word "air" from the names of several freight divisions following an action by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission which found TNT was in the practice of indicating goods were being transported by air when in fact they were being carried by road and by doing so, breaching the Trade Practices Act. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Ahead of this morning's monthly Reserve Bank board meeting, leading economists yesterday predicted that the time was right for a cut in interest rates. However, comments by Prime Minister John Howard yesterday appeared to weaken the case for an immediate rate cut. Page 1.

Following an animated board meeting yesterday, Australian National Industries chairman Ted Harris announced the group had dumped the board committee in charge of investigating the ill-fated ABT investment and appointed leading QC Bob Ellicott to head an independent inquiry. Page 25.

In a move which follows the successful strategy of the cheap non-bank lenders, Westpac has announced plans to go straight into the money market to raise A$340 million to finance its no-frills "basic option" home loans. It is a move which could lower home loan interest rates and lead to another share buy-back. Page 25.

Coles Myer vice chairman Solomon Lew as well as aides Harry Cooper and Monica Vinson have accused the Australian Securities Commission of allowing Peter Hiland, one of its officers, to give confidential transcripts of confidential interviews to Coles Myer even though a settlement of the Yannon dispute was imminent. Page 27.

After posting a disappointing A$61.8 million net loss after abnormals for the year to June 30, diversified food ingredient group Burns Philp has identified an improvement in efficiency and a tight control on costs across all its operations as the main goas for the financial year. Page 27.

Goodman Fielder released its draft 1996 annual report to the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday, which predicts another tough year ahead. Goodman chairman David Clarke says in the report the company is still not extracting an adequate return from assets, but that the year was one of important change for the company. Page 27.
THE AGE

Pacific BBA has secured contracts valued at more than A$200 million a year to supply U.S. manufacturers with automotive components, significantly lifting the group's presence in the U.S. auto supply market. The size of the contract will require the group to bild a A$100 million factory on the U.S. mid-east coast. Page C1.

In documents filed with Melbourne's Federal Court, a Coles Myer director, Solomon Lew and two of his aides, Harry Cooper and Monica Vinson, have alleged the Australian Securities Commission deliberately kept one of its officers ignorant about the Yannon dipute settlement. Page C1.

Mining giant WMC managing director Hugh Morgan has received a significant pay increase. In the annual report which details the salaries of its executive directors for the first time, Morgan's total remuneration in 1995/96 increased to A$995,186 from A$790,145 in 1994/95. Page C1.

Australian National Industries has off-loaded the board committee charged with the investigation of the ABT investment. ANI has instead opted to appoint prominent QC Bob Ellicott to head an independent inquiry into the deal. Page C2.

Japanese computer game giant Sega Enterprises has formed a joint venture with Village Nine Leisure, valued at A$7 million. Under the agreement, VNL has obtained the exclusive distribution of Sega's arcade games in Australasia. Page C2.

Mining giant RTZ-CRA subsidiary Hamersley Iron has announced the signing of a contract which sees the group supplying more than 32 million tonnes of iron ore over 10 years to Taiwan's China Steel Corp. The A$800 million contract will come into force next April and expires in March 2007. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
